title: Count VaR exceedances from given VaR forecasts and returns
frame: DIKETAHUI: returns r [T], VaR forecasts VaR_t [T] (positive), level c, aligned by date. DITANYAKAN: hit indicators, count x, rate x/T, expected pT. RUMUS: card Core 1, V1(a): I_t = 1{-r_t > VaR_t} = 1{r_t < -VaR_t}; x = sum I; p = 1-c; toolkit exceedances(r, var_series, strict=True). JAWAB: 1) align by date (inner join). 2) sign convention: VaR positive. 3) hits. 4) x, x/T, pT. 5) cast numpy ints/bools to python in JSON.
pitfalls: VaR given as negative quantile compared with wrong sign

title: Exceedances with non-strict rule (loss >= VaR)
frame: DIKETAHUI: returns r [T], VaR [T]; text says loss >= VaR counts. DITANYAKAN: violation count under the stated rule. RUMUS: card V1(b): I_t = 1{L_t >= VaR_t}; toolkit exceedances(..., strict=False); ties occur with HS order-statistic VaR on overlapping data. JAWAB: 1) hits under both rules. 2) report the one stated. 3) note tie count.

title: Kupiec proportion-of-failures test
deliverables: summary json: x, T, lr_uc, p_value, reject
frame: DIKETAHUI: hits [T] or (x, T), level c, significance a. DITANYAKAN: LR_uc, p-value, reject flag. RUMUS: card Core 2: p = 1-c; phat = x/T; LR_uc = -2[(T-x) ln(1-p) + x ln p] + 2[(T-x) ln(1-phat) + x ln phat]; p-value = chi2.sf(LR,1); reject if p-value < a; toolkit kupiec_pof(x, T, level=c). JAWAB: 1) x, T. 2) LR with 0 ln 0 = 0. 3) sf. 4) decision. 5) check LR >= 0.

title: Kupiec test edge case with zero violations
frame: DIKETAHUI: T forecast days, x = 0, c. DITANYAKAN: finite LR_uc and p-value. RUMUS: card Core 2, Invariants: with x = 0, LR_uc = -2T ln(1-p) (second bracket vanishes by 0 ln 0 = 0); x = T: LR = -2T ln p. JAWAB: 1) use xlogy-safe terms. 2) compute LR. 3) p-value. 4) note test rejects 'too few' violations too (two-sided).

title: Exact binomial backtest of violation count
frame: DIKETAHUI: x, T, c, sidedness. DITANYAKAN: exact binomial p-value. RUMUS: card V6(b): X ~ Bin(T, p); one-sided upper p-value = P(X >= x) = binom.sf(x-1, T, p); two-sided via scipy.stats.binomtest(x, T, p). JAWAB: 1) p = 1-c. 2) one- or two-sided per text. 3) p-value. 4) decision.
pitfalls: binom.sf(x) gives P(X > x), not P(X >= x)

title: Normal-approximation (z) test of violation frequency
frame: DIKETAHUI: x, T, c. DITANYAKAN: z statistic and p-value. RUMUS: card Core 5: z = (x - pT)/sqrt(p(1-p)T); two-sided p = 2 norm.sf(|z|); reject if |z| > z_{1-a/2}. JAWAB: 1) expected and std. 2) z. 3) p-value. 4) decision.

title: Christoffersen independence test from a hit sequence
deliverables: summary json: n00, n01, n10, n11, pi01, pi11, lr_ind, p_value
frame: DIKETAHUI: hits [T] (0/1 in time order). DITANYAKAN: transition counts, LR_ind, p-value. RUMUS: card Core 3: pairs (I_{t-1}, I_t), t = 2..T (T-1 pairs); pi01 = n01/(n00+n01), pi11 = n11/(n10+n11), pi = (n01+n11)/(T-1); LR_ind = -2[ln L(pi) - ln L(pi01, pi11)]; toolkit christoffersen_independence(hits). JAWAB: 1) counts via zip(h[:-1], h[1:]). 2) probabilities (0 ln 0 = 0 when n10+n11 = 0). 3) LR, chi2.sf(LR,1). 4) check counts sum to T-1.

title: Christoffersen conditional coverage test
deliverables: summary json: lr_uc, lr_ind, lr_cc, p_value_cc
frame: DIKETAHUI: hits [T], c. DITANYAKAN: LR_cc and p-value (chi2 with 2 df). RUMUS: card Core 4: LR_cc = LR_uc + LR_ind; p = chi2.sf(LR_cc, 2); toolkit christoffersen_cc(hits, level=c). JAWAB: 1) LR_uc on T days. 2) LR_ind on T-1 pairs. 3) sum. 4) p-value. 5) decision at a (5.991 critical at 5%).

title: Christoffersen tests from given transition counts only
frame: DIKETAHUI: n00, n01, n10, n11 (no hit series), c; optionally first hit value. DITANYAKAN: LR_ind, LR_uc, LR_cc. RUMUS: card Core 2-4: T-1 = sum n_ij; x approximately n01 + n11 (+ first-day hit if given); LR_uc on T = sum n_ij + 1 with x as above. JAWAB: 1) reconstruct T and x (state assumption). 2) LR_ind. 3) LR_uc. 4) LR_cc and p-values.

title: Basel traffic light zone and plus factor
deliverables: summary json: exceptions, zone, plus_factor, multiplier
frame: DIKETAHUI: exceptions x over the last 250 days at 99% VaR. DITANYAKAN: zone, plus factor k, multiplier 3+k. RUMUS: card Core 6: green 0-4, yellow 5-9, red >= 10; k: 0-4 -> 0, 5 .40, 6 .50, 7 .65, 8 .75, 9 .85, >= 10 1.0; toolkit basel_traffic_light(x, n=250, level=0.99). JAWAB: 1) count on most recent 250 days. 2) zone. 3) k. 4) multiplier.

title: Basel capital charge from VaR series and backtesting multiplier
deliverables: summary json: k, multiplier, mean_var_60, capital
frame: DIKETAHUI: 1-day or 10-day VaR series [>= 60], exceptions over 250 days. DITANYAKAN: capital requirement. RUMUS: card Core 6: Capital = max(VaR_{t-1}, (3+k) mean(VaR over last 60 days)); use 10-day VaR = sqrt(10) VaR_1 when the text says so. JAWAB: 1) k from traffic light. 2) last VaR and 60-day mean. 3) max. 4) currency.

title: Traffic-light zone boundaries from cumulative binomial for non-standard sample
frame: DIKETAHUI: number of days n, level c. DITANYAKAN: zone thresholds as exception counts. RUMUS: card Core 6: P(X <= x), X ~ Bin(n, 1-c); green while cum < 0.95, yellow while cum < 0.9999, red after. JAWAB: 1) cdf over x = 0..n. 2) first x with cum >= 0.95 starts yellow; first with cum >= 0.9999 starts red. 3) table.

title: Rolling-window historical VaR backtest end to end
deliverables: summary json: x, lr_uc, lr_ind, lr_cc, p-values
frame: DIKETAHUI: returns r [N] dated, window W, level c. DITANYAKAN: out-of-sample VaR series, hits, tests. RUMUS: card Core 7, V7(a): for t = W..N-1, VaR_t = HS VaR of r[t-W:t]; hit_t = 1{r_t < -VaR_t}; T = N - W; toolkit historical_var_es, exceedances, kupiec_pof, christoffersen_cc. JAWAB: 1) sort. 2) loop windows (no look-ahead). 3) hits. 4) tests. 5) check len = N - W, LR_cc = LR_uc + LR_ind.
pitfalls: including r_t in its own window

title: Expanding-window VaR backtest
frame: DIKETAHUI: returns r [N], minimum m, c, method. DITANYAKAN: VaR for t = m..N-1 using r[0:t], hits, tests. RUMUS: card Core 7, V2(b): T = N - m forecasts. JAWAB: 1) loop t from m. 2) VaR from r[:t]. 3) hits. 4) tests. 5) check count.

title: Parametric normal rolling VaR backtest
frame: DIKETAHUI: returns r [N], W, c, mean convention. DITANYAKAN: rolling normal VaR, hits, Kupiec/Christoffersen. RUMUS: card Core 7 + var-es Core 3: VaR_t = z_c std(r[t-W:t], ddof=1) - mean(...); toolkit parametric_var_es per window. JAWAB: 1) rolling mean/std shifted by one. 2) VaR. 3) hits. 4) tests.
pitfalls: pandas rolling without shift(1) includes day t

title: EWMA (RiskMetrics) VaR backtest
frame: DIKETAHUI: returns r [N], lambda, seed rule, burn-in, c. DITANYAKAN: EWMA VaR series for out-of-sample days, hits, tests. RUMUS: card Conventions + volatility Core 1: sigma2_t uses returns through t-1; VaR_t = z_c sigma_t (zero mean); evaluate from the stated start (after burn-in). JAWAB: 1) recursion. 2) align forecast to day t. 3) hits. 4) tests.

title: Filtered-HS or GARCH VaR backtest
frame: DIKETAHUI: returns r [N], vol model and window, c. DITANYAKAN: VaR series and backtest statistics. RUMUS: card Core 7 + var-es Core 6: per t, sigma forecast from data < t, FHS quantile of standardized residuals of the window times sigma_t. JAWAB: 1) window loop. 2) sigma and scenarios. 3) VaR_t. 4) hits. 5) tests; expect lower LR_ind than plain HS.

title: Multi-level backtest table (95% and 99%)
deliverables: table rows (level, x, T, rate, expected, lr_uc, p_value)
frame: DIKETAHUI: returns [N], method, W, levels [C]. DITANYAKAN: one backtest row per level. RUMUS: card Core 1-4 per level. JAWAB: 1) VaR series per level. 2) hits. 3) tests. 4) check x_99 <= x_95.

title: Backtest comparison across VaR models
deliverables: table rows (model, x, rate, lr_uc, lr_ind, lr_cc, p values)
frame: DIKETAHUI: returns [N], list of models, W, c. DITANYAKAN: backtest statistics per model and the preferred model. RUMUS: card Core 1-4; tie-break by LR_cc p-value or by a stated loss (e.g. quantile/tick loss sum (p - I_t)(r_t + VaR_t)). JAWAB: 1) VaR series per model on common days. 2) tests. 3) rank. 4) report.

title: Quantile (tick) loss scoring of VaR forecasts
frame: DIKETAHUI: returns r [T], VaR forecasts per model, c. DITANYAKAN: average quantile loss per model. RUMUS: Giacomini-Komunjer: q_t = -VaR_t; loss = (p - 1{r_t < q_t})(r_t - q_t), p = 1-c; lower is better. JAWAB: 1) q_t. 2) loss per day. 3) mean per model. 4) rank.

title: Expected shortfall backtest (Acerbi-Szekely Z2)
frame: DIKETAHUI: returns r [T], VaR_t [T], ES_t [T] (positive), c. DITANYAKAN: Z2 statistic (expected 0 under correct ES, negative when ES underestimated). RUMUS: Acerbi-Szekely 2014: Z2 = sum_t r_t I_t/(T p ES_t) + 1, I_t = 1{r_t < -VaR_t}, p = 1-c. JAWAB: 1) hits. 2) sum of r_t I_t/ES_t. 3) Z2. 4) compare with simulated or tabulated critical value if given.
formulas: Z2 = sum_t r_t I_t/(T p ES_t) + 1

title: Violation durations and clustering summary
frame: DIKETAHUI: hits [T] with dates, c. DITANYAKAN: dates of violations, durations, mean vs 1/p. RUMUS: Christoffersen-Pelletier: durations d_i = t_i - t_{i-1} in trading days; mean should be near 1/p under correct coverage and independence. JAWAB: 1) indices of hits. 2) diffs. 3) mean, max. 4) ISO dates.

title: Violation counts by calendar year or rolling 250-day block
frame: DIKETAHUI: hits [T] with dates. DITANYAKAN: exceptions per year (or per 250-day block) and zones. RUMUS: card Core 6: groupby(date.year).sum(); for rolling: hits.rolling(250).sum() at each date. JAWAB: 1) dates parsed. 2) group or roll. 3) zones per period (250-day only for standard zones).

title: Rejection region of Kupiec test (critical violation counts)
frame: DIKETAHUI: T, c, significance a. DITANYAKAN: range of x for which Kupiec is not rejected. RUMUS: card Core 2: evaluate LR_uc(x) for x = 0..T; non-rejection set {x : LR_uc(x) < chi2.ppf(1-a, 1)} (3.841 at 5%). JAWAB: 1) vector of LR. 2) threshold. 3) min and max accepted x.

title: Deduplicate dates keeping last occurrence before sorting
frame: DIKETAHUI: raw rows [n_raw] (date, symbol, price) in file order. DITANYAKAN: cleaned rows and number removed. RUMUS: card Conventions, V5(a): df.drop_duplicates(subset=[date, symbol], keep='last') in original file order, THEN sort by date. JAWAB: 1) parse dates first so equal dates in different formats match. 2) drop duplicates. 3) count. 4) sort.
pitfalls: sorting first changes which row survives

title: Parse mixed date formats per value
frame: DIKETAHUI: date strings in several formats (%Y-%m-%d, %m/%d/%Y, %d-%b-%y, %Y%m%d). DITANYAKAN: canonical YYYY-MM-DD dates, zero NaT. RUMUS: card Conventions: try explicit formats in order per value; slash dates US month-first unless day > 12 or text says day-first; assert no NaT. JAWAB: 1) strip whitespace. 2) per-value parser. 3) canonical string. 4) count failures (must be 0).
pitfalls: single pd.to_datetime infers one format and NaTs the rest

title: Filter rows against a supplied trading calendar
frame: DIKETAHUI: rows with dates, calendar list [n_cal]. DITANYAKAN: rows restricted to calendar dates and count removed. RUMUS: card Conventions: compare canonical YYYY-MM-DD strings (set membership); do not generate holidays. JAWAB: 1) canonicalise both sides. 2) isin. 3) count removed. 4) continue cleaning order.
pitfalls: Timestamp vs string comparison silently fails

title: Remove weekend rows
frame: DIKETAHUI: dated rows; no calendar supplied, text says weekends are non-trading. DITANYAKAN: rows without weekends, count removed. RUMUS: card Conventions: dayofweek >= 5 removed. JAWAB: 1) parse dates. 2) filter. 3) count.

title: Absolute-threshold outlier removal on returns (NaN-safe)
frame: DIKETAHUI: returns r (may include NaN), threshold x. DITANYAKAN: rows with |r| > x removed, count. RUMUS: card Conventions: mask = r.abs() > x (NaN -> False, removed later by the missing step); follow stated step order (outlier test on returns, then drop row or price). JAWAB: 1) compute returns as stated. 2) mask. 3) remove. 4) count. 5) recompute returns if prices were removed and the text says so.

title: Robust MAD outlier filter
frame: DIKETAHUI: returns r [T], multiplier k. DITANYAKAN: flagged outliers and cleaned series. RUMUS: card Conventions: |r - median| > k 1.4826 MAD, MAD = median(|r - median|). JAWAB: 1) median. 2) MAD. 3) mask. 4) remove and count.

title: Stale price runs treated as missing
frame: DIKETAHUI: price series per symbol, minimum run length L. DITANYAKAN: stale rows flagged and set missing. RUMUS: card Conventions: groups of consecutive equal prices of length >= L; mark all but the first (or all, as stated) as missing; do not create zero returns. JAWAB: 1) run id via (p != p.shift()).cumsum(). 2) run lengths. 3) mark. 4) count.

title: Missing values: listwise deletion across assets
frame: DIKETAHUI: wide prices [T x N] with NaN. DITANYAKAN: aligned dates with no NaN in any asset. RUMUS: card V4(a): df.dropna(how='any'); then returns on consecutive remaining rows. JAWAB: 1) dropna across all columns. 2) count. 3) returns. 4) note returns may span the gap.
formulas: keep rows with all N prices present

title: Forward-fill prices when stated
frame: DIKETAHUI: wide prices with gaps; text says forward-fill prices. DITANYAKAN: filled prices and resulting returns. RUMUS: card V4(b): prices.ffill() (limit if given); returns after filling (zero returns on filled days); leading NaN remain and are dropped. JAWAB: 1) ffill. 2) drop leading NaN. 3) returns. 4) count filled cells.

title: Invalid and non-positive prices removed
frame: DIKETAHUI: price rows (possibly strings, zero, negative). DITANYAKAN: rows with valid positive numeric price. RUMUS: card Conventions: pd.to_numeric(errors='coerce'); drop <= 0 before taking logs; count separately from missing if steps differ. JAWAB: 1) coerce. 2) mask <= 0. 3) remove. 4) count.

title: Percent strings and percent-scale returns converted to decimals
frame: DIKETAHUI: returns column as strings like '1.2%' or numbers in percent. DITANYAKAN: decimal returns. RUMUS: card Conventions: strip '%', to_numeric, divide by 100; numeric percent detection when |r| > 1 routinely. JAWAB: 1) detect. 2) convert. 3) verify typical |r| < 0.2 for daily data.

title: Adjusted close preferred; split adjustment from split ratios
frame: DIKETAHUI: close prices, adjusted close (if present) or split events (date, ratio). DITANYAKAN: split-consistent prices and returns. RUMUS: card Conventions: use adjusted close if available; else divide prices before the split date by the ratio (cumulative product of later ratios). JAWAB: 1) factor_t = prod ratios with date > t. 2) adjusted = close/factor. 3) returns. 4) check no artificial jump at split.

title: Total return series with dividends
frame: DIKETAHUI: prices P [T+1], dividends D_t on ex-dates. DITANYAKAN: daily total returns. RUMUS: Standard: r_t = (P_t + D_t)/P_{t-1} - 1 on ex-date; price return otherwise. JAWAB: 1) align dividends to dates. 2) returns. 3) cumulative total return prod(1+r) - 1.

title: Long format pivot to wide with inner-join counts
deliverables: summary json: rows per symbol, n_common_dates, n_returns
frame: DIKETAHUI: rows (date, symbol, price). DITANYAKAN: wide prices [T+1 x N] on common dates and count summary. RUMUS: card Conventions: pivot_table(aggfunc='last') if duplicates remain; dropna(how='any'); returns = dates - 1. JAWAB: 1) per-symbol counts. 2) pivot. 3) align. 4) returns.

title: Ordered cleaning pipeline with audit counts
frame: DIKETAHUI: raw file rows, ordered list of steps (parse, dedupe, calendar, invalid, outlier, missing, stale). DITANYAKAN: per-step removal counts and final rows. RUMUS: card Worked frame, Invariants: count raw from the file; each step counts rows removed among rows still present; final = raw - sum removed. JAWAB: 1) apply steps exactly in stated order. 2) record counts. 3) assert identity. 4) emit audit table.

title: Simple versus log returns conversion and comparison
frame: DIKETAHUI: prices P [T+1]. DITANYAKAN: both return series and conversion. RUMUS: card Core 9: r = P_t/P_{t-1} - 1; l = ln(P_t/P_{t-1}) = ln(1+r); time aggregation: log sums, simple compounds; cross-sectional: simple weights. JAWAB: 1) both series via pct_change(fill_method=None) and np.log. 2) consistency check l = log1p(r).

title: Equal-weight daily-rebalanced portfolio returns
frame: DIKETAHUI: asset returns R [T x N]. DITANYAKAN: portfolio return series. RUMUS: card Core 8: w = 1/N; r_p = R.mean(axis=1) on simple returns. JAWAB: 1) aligned simple returns. 2) mean across columns. 3) if log requested, apply variant explicitly.

title: Buy-and-hold portfolio with drifting weights
frame: DIKETAHUI: prices [T+1 x N], initial weights w0 or shares n, initial capital V0. DITANYAKAN: portfolio value path and returns. RUMUS: card Core 8: n_i = w0_i V0/P_i,0; V_t = sum n_i P_i,t; r_p,t = V_t/V_{t-1} - 1; weights w_t = n_i P_i,t/V_t. JAWAB: 1) shares. 2) value path. 3) returns. 4) compare with rebalanced if asked.
pitfalls: applying fixed weights to returns (that is rebalancing)

title: Portfolio P&L in currency from positions
frame: DIKETAHUI: positions (shares) [N], prices [T+1 x N] (or position values and returns). DITANYAKAN: daily P&L in currency. RUMUS: card Core 8: PnL_t = sum n_i (P_i,t - P_i,t-1) (actual) or sum x_i r_i,t (hypothetical, fixed values). JAWAB: 1) choose actual vs hypothetical per text. 2) compute. 3) summary statistics.

title: Log portfolio return ln(sum w e^r) from asset log returns
frame: DIKETAHUI: asset log returns L [T x N], weights w. DITANYAKAN: portfolio log return series. RUMUS: card Core 9: r_p = ln(sum w_i exp(L_i)); not the weighted average unless text says average. JAWAB: 1) exp. 2) weighted sum. 3) log. 4) report difference vs weighted average.

title: Historical stress scenario P&L
frame: DIKETAHUI: positions x [N] (currency), scenario returns [S x N] (or historical dates to replay). DITANYAKAN: P&L per scenario and worst scenario. RUMUS: card Invariants: stress P&L_s = sum_i x_i r_s,i; full reval for options if given. JAWAB: 1) build scenario matrix (dates or specified shocks). 2) multiply. 3) rank.

title: Worst-day and summary statistics of a cleaned return series
deliverables: summary json: worst_date, worst_return, mean, std, skew, kurt
frame: DIKETAHUI: cleaned returns with dates. DITANYAKAN: descriptive statistics. RUMUS: card Invariants: worst date as zero-padded ISO string; std ddof=1; skew/kurt (excess) as stated. JAWAB: 1) idxmin. 2) stats. 3) cast types for JSON. 4) check worst <= -VaR_99.

title: Returns across gaps: pct_change fill_method pitfall
frame: DIKETAHUI: prices with NaN gaps. DITANYAKAN: correct returns without fabricated zeros. RUMUS: card Conventions: pct_change(fill_method=None) gives NaN around gaps; listwise-drop first if the return should span the gap. JAWAB: 1) choose policy. 2) compute. 3) count NaN. 4) drop.
formulas: r_t = P_t/P_{t-1} - 1 on consecutive valid rows
pitfalls: old default padded NaN creating zero returns

title: Intraday timestamps normalised to trading dates
frame: DIKETAHUI: timestamped prices (possibly multiple per day, time zones). DITANYAKAN: one end-of-day price per date. RUMUS: Standard: convert to the exchange time zone, dt.normalize() or dt.date, take last observation per day (groupby date .last()). JAWAB: 1) tz handling. 2) group. 3) last price. 4) proceed to returns.
formulas: P_day = last price of the day

title: Convert foreign-currency prices to base currency before returns
frame: DIKETAHUI: prices in local currencies [T x N], FX rates [T x K], currency map. DITANYAKAN: base-currency prices and returns. RUMUS: Standard: P_base = P_local * X (base per local) aligned by date; returns (1+r_local)(1+r_fx) - 1. JAWAB: 1) align FX dates. 2) invert quotes if needed. 3) multiply. 4) returns.

title: Align returns and VaR forecasts by date before testing
frame: DIKETAHUI: returns dated, VaR forecasts dated (as-of date or target date). DITANYAKAN: aligned pairs for testing. RUMUS: card V7: if VaR stamped at estimation date t-1, shift forward one row so it pairs with r_t; inner join on target date. JAWAB: 1) determine stamping convention. 2) shift. 3) join. 4) count T.

title: Hypothetical versus actual P&L backtest
frame: DIKETAHUI: VaR series, positions held fixed, actual P&L series (including trading, fees). DITANYAKAN: violation counts under both P&L definitions. RUMUS: Basel 1996: hypothetical P&L = end-of-day positions revalued next day; actual includes intraday trading and fees. JAWAB: 1) build both. 2) hits. 3) tests for each.

title: Rolling Kupiec test over consecutive 250-day blocks
deliverables: table rows (block start, x, lr_uc, p_value)
frame: DIKETAHUI: hits [T], block length B, c. DITANYAKAN: Kupiec per block. RUMUS: card Core 2 per block hits[k B:(k+1) B]. JAWAB: 1) blocks (drop partial or keep as stated). 2) LR per block. 3) table.

title: Winsorization of returns at quantiles
frame: DIKETAHUI: returns r [T], lower/upper quantiles. DITANYAKAN: winsorized series. RUMUS: Standard: clip(r, Q_lo, Q_hi) with np.quantile linear; trimming instead removes rows (different count). JAWAB: 1) bounds. 2) clip. 3) count changed values.

title: Normalise symbols and column names before pivot
frame: DIKETAHUI: rows with symbol variants (case, spaces), column name variants. DITANYAKAN: consistent symbol keys matching weights. RUMUS: Standard: str.strip().str.upper(); rename columns to canonical (date, symbol, price); map weights by symbol. JAWAB: 1) normalise. 2) verify all weight keys present. 3) pivot.

title: Backtest JSON output types and rounding
frame: DIKETAHUI: computed statistics (numpy types). DITANYAKAN: JSON-safe outputs. RUMUS: card Pitfalls: cast np.int64 -> int, np.bool_ -> bool, np.float64 -> float; dates as ISO strings; NaN -> null. JAWAB: 1) cast. 2) json.dump. 3) re-load to verify.

title: Backtest of an HS VaR on current holdings (constant positions)
frame: DIKETAHUI: positions x [N] (currency), returns R [N_days x N], window W, c. DITANYAKAN: P&L-based VaR backtest. RUMUS: card Core 8 + Core 7: PnL_t = R_t x; VaR_t = -Q_{1-c}(PnL_{t-W..t-1}); hit if PnL_t < -VaR_t. JAWAB: 1) P&L series. 2) rolling VaR. 3) hits. 4) tests.
